title: I Played 30 AI-Assisted Indie Games. Here Are Some Worth Trying.
author: Square-Yam-3772
selftext:
After reviewing 30 games submitted by fellow developers, I wanted to share a few that I think are worth checking out from a player's perspective.

These aren't necessarily the highest-scoring games. I picked them because I think they offer something worthwhile to someone actually looking for a game to play.

**Scrapfit** \[browser, [https://straydreamarts.itch.io/scrapfit-dev](https://straydreamarts.itch.io/scrapfit-dev)\]

If you enjoy turn-based dungeon crawlers and inventory-management games, give this one a try.

The Tetris-like inventory pieces function as your skills, which adds an interesting layer to combat. More importantly, everything feels well put together. The combat is satisfying, the presentation is polished, and there's a Slay the Spire-style progression map with a reasonable amount of content.

It's free and playable in your browser, so there's very little barrier to giving it a shot.

**Nightshoal** \[windows only, [https://profactor.itch.io/nightshoal](https://profactor.itch.io/nightshoal)\]

If you have fond memories of old PC games from the CD-ROM era, this might be right up your alley.

It's a fishing game with exploration, a grid-based inventory system, and surprisingly good visuals. The retro aesthetic is especially convincing, and there's more to do than simply cast a fishing line.

This one impressed me because it feels like an actual game taking shape rather than a quick prototype. Particularly worth checking out if you enjoy relaxed fishing games.

**Ascend from Nine Mountains** \[Steam, https://store.steampowered.com/app/3992260/Ascend\_From\_Nine\_Mountains\]

If you're looking for something closer to a traditional commercial game, this is one of the more substantial projects I've encountered.

It's an Asian-mythology-inspired autobattler with a polished introduction, good audio, and a decent amount of gameplay systems. There's clearly a lot of work behind it.

I don't play many autobattlers myself, but if you enjoy the genre, this looks like a promising one to explore.

**Strain** \[browser, [https://w.run/chopjohn/strain](https://w.run/chopjohn/strain)\]

If you enjoy incremental games and watching systems gradually develop, this is worth a look.

You essentially play as a scientist experimenting with a petri dish. The premise is interesting, the interface works well, and the game makes an effort to incorporate actual scientific concepts.

I don't know how long the progression ultimately lasts, but the core experience is polished enough that I think incremental-game fans could have some fun with it.

**Transportit** \[browser, [https://fabianxr.itch.io/transportit](https://fabianxr.itch.io/transportit)\]

If you enjoy city planning or experimenting with procedural systems, this one offers something a little different.

Instead of building a traditional city, you're working with procedurally generated urban layouts. The concept is refreshingly unusual, and the underlying systems appear to function well.

It's probably not something everyone will spend hours playing, but if you like experimenting with cities and planning systems, I think it's worth trying.

**Under Training** \[browser, [https://under-training.vercel.app/](https://under-training.vercel.app/)\]

If you prefer short, atmospheric, story-driven experiences, this one is particularly interesting.

You play as an AI model undergoing training. The art direction, music, and presentation work together exceptionally well, and there's some token-based gameplay to accompany the narrative.

Don't go in expecting a lengthy game with deep mechanics. Think of it more as a short interactive experience with a distinctive atmosphere.

**A few more worth considering:**

* **SumMon** \[Steam, [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5130400/SumMon](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5130400/SumMon/)\]**:** For fans of old-school fantasy strategy and turn-based monster battles. The demo looks polished and provides a good introduction to its systems.
* **Energize** \[browser, [https://hotrod462.itch.io/energize](https://hotrod462.itch.io/energize)\]**:** For players interested in simulator games, especially technology and infrastructure. The presentation is surprisingly professional, complete with cutscenes and voiceovers.
* **Spirestorm** \[browser, [https://nextgenrungames.itch.io/spirestorm](https://nextgenrungames.itch.io/spirestorm)\]**:** For players who enjoy straightforward climbing challenges. The core idea isn't particularly new, but the movement feels good and the production quality is strong.
* **Cardboard Conquest** \[Steam, [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4937370/Cardboard\_Conquest](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4937370/Cardboard_Conquest/)\]: A lane-based autobattler with a charming cardboard aesthetic and one of the most bizarre music selections I've ever encountered.

These recommendations are based on my first impressions, not full playthroughs. Your experience may differ depending on your preferred genres.

I've also posted gameplay footage and more detailed reviews on my [YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/@DepartmentOfSlopReviews) if you'd like to see the games in action.

Thanks to everyone who has submitted their games so far! I'm still working my way through the submission list, so there are plenty more games to come.
